title: A Technical Guide to Mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate
content_md: Executive Summary Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in HotSpot’s AVX-512 Base64 decoder on x86-64. Calif reported it and showed pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Nobody has reported exploitation in the wild as of November 17, 2026. CISA issued an alert that same day, urging everyone to patch now. Your Java4Shell Response Plan Patch to Oracle 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, or 27.0.1.1, or to your vendor’s build with JDK-8393212. If you can’t patch today, start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restart it. You’re only exposed on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI. ARM64 isn’t affected. Tip for Qualys customers: you can apply the step 2 flag with TruRisk Eliminate, targeting only the hosts that need it and rolling it back in one click. Affected Java Builds and Their Fixed Releases Oracle shipped the fixed builds on November 17, 2026. October’s builds are still vulnerable. Product Range Vulnerable Fixed build (Oracle) Oracle Java SE / OpenJDK 17 17.0.6 to 17.0.21 17.0.21.1 Oracle Java SE / OpenJDK 21 Below 21.0.13.1 21.0.13.1 Oracle Java SE / OpenJDK 25 Below 25.0.5.1 25.0.5.1 Oracle Java SE / OpenJDK 27 Below 27.0.1.1 27.0.1.1 OpenJDK (end of life) 18 to 20, 22 to 24, 26 All None. Move to a supported line Oracle Java SE 8 Enterprise Performance Pack 8 8u511-perf 8u513-perf Oracle GraalVM for JDK 17 / 21 Below the fix 17.0.21.1 / 21.0.13.1 Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3 Below the fix 21.3.20.
